chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Abi Said al-Qammat and Salih ibn Said, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a matter and he answered it,

The man said: 'The jurists do not say this.' He said: 'Woe be upon you! Have you ever seen a true Faqih? A true Faqih is one who renounces the world, desires the Hereafter, and holds firmly to the Sunnah of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.الْفَقِيهَ: The jurist/scholar (singular, implying the ideal type)
key_terms.الْفُقَهَاءَ: The jurists (plural of Faqih, often referring to scholars of fiqh)

ai.seo_question: What are the defining characteristics of a true Faqih (jurist) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) corrects the common perception of 'jurists' (Fuqaha) by defining the true 'Faqih' as one who is detached from the worldly life, eager for the Hereafter, and strictly adheres to the Prophet's Sunnah. This hadith emphasizes that true religious authority is rooted in piety and adherence to prophetic tradition rather than mere technical legal knowledge.
